A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Durian and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. Inspection covered all supplied pages, including v1's appendices A-C and Figures 8-12. The supplied v3 ends with references and contains no appended supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, component ablations and qualitative animation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds quantitative cross-identity attribute-transfer results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The dual-reference architecture, training objectives, mask expansion, attention, composition and interpolation procedures are retained. Face Aligner describes the existing GAGAvatar/EMOCA alignment process. Added prompt-generation details and omitted appendix preparation recipes change documentation without establishing a revised underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: The datasets remain CelebV-Text, VFHQ and Nersemble. Cross-identity transfer was already demonstrated qualitatively in v1. Coverage changes modestly: v3 omits the text-generated hairstyle-reference scenario from v1 Appendix B/Figure 8 and adds hat interpolation in Figure 7.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same four editors crossed with LivePortrait, X-Portrait and MegActor-Sigma. Qualitative comparisons narrow from four editors with X-Portrait in v1 Figure 4, plus the broader appendix grid, to StableHair with X-Portrait in v3 Figure 4. Its caption and labels identify X-Portrait despite the results paragraph naming LivePortrait.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 50-video quantitative cross-attribute protocol using different identities, with mCLIP-I, mDINO, ArcFace identity similarity and I3D/ResNeXt VFID metrics. v1's quantitative evaluation used 200 self-transfer videos and reconstruction/perceptual-image metrics; that evaluation is retained. This substantially extends the evaluation design beyond reconstruction.

E4.justification: The five component ablations, Table 2 measurements and Figure 5 examples are unchanged. Figure 7 extends the qualitative feature-interpolation analysis to hats, supplementing the existing hair, beard and eyeglasses examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new cross-transfer results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 65 existing Table 1 values and all 24 Table 2 values are unchanged. v3 adds cross-transfer results, with Durian leading four of five metrics. Its ResNeXt VFID of 2.4052 is worse than StableHair plus MegActor-Sigma at 1.4672. Figure 4 supplies a different cross-identity comparison, while several appendix demonstrations disappear from the supplied document.

T1.justification: The attention equations, diffusion losses, mask unions and interpolation formula are mathematically equivalent across versions. Equations are consolidated, moved inline and renumbered; no substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim zero-shot portrait animation with cross-identity attribute transfer, learning without triplet supervision, and single-pass composition and interpolation. v3 foregrounds interpolation and Dual ReferenceNet in its abstract and contribution list, but these capabilities and contributions were already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies self-transfer evaluation as primarily measuring reconstruction rather than full cross-identity transfer. Conversely, it removes v1's concrete limitations concerning overlapping attributes, lighting discrepancies, extreme poses and keypoint/tracking failures. Appendix A's explanation of guidance-induced facial-shape leakage is also absent, materially reducing the stated failure boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 documents automatic prompt generation through sampled attribute modifiers, clarifies that reference encoders exclude temporal layers, and explicitly states code availability at the project page. It omits v1's LivePortrait-to-Sapiens motion-guidance preparation instructions and FLUX text-generated-reference recipe. These are disclosure changes; implementation or online availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against 3D attribute-transfer work, including PEGASUS, PERSE, GALA, DeClotH, MEGA and HairCUP, and introduces MEGANE in the motivation. It also adds references supporting the new evaluation metrics. The central positioning against separate editing and animation approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around training-data scarcity, complementary masking and compositional capabilities. Contributions are reorganized, method explanations are streamlined, and Discussion becomes Conclusion with acknowledgments. The earlier appendices are absent from v3.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and moved before the abstract; Figure 3 simplifies the alignment diagram. Table 1 becomes a full-width comparison with two evaluation groups, Figure 4 is replaced, and Figures 5-7 receive substantially larger layouts and clearer reference displays. Figure 7 adds a hat row; appendix Figures 8-12 are absent.

improvement.justification: The new cross-identity quantitative evaluation strengthens evidence for the central application beyond v1's reconstruction-only numerical comparisons, and v3 clearly explains that distinction. However, removing concrete failure limitations and motion-guidance instructions weakens transparency and reproducibility, while Figure 4 introduces a baseline-label inconsistency. These losses limit the overall gain.
